provenance: Computed by the LunarWindow pipeline from NASA LOLA terrain and NASA SPICE (DE421) ephemerides. Code written with AI assistance (Claude Code) and verified by the team with automated tests and a comparison against NASA PGDA illumination maps.
verdict: Touchdown 2028-10-24T17 UTC: the Sun's centre is 2.10 deg above the skyline and the top of Earth's disc 0.04 deg above the skyline (power and a link at landing).
Over 14 days: Sun up 97%, Earth in view 99%, both 96% of the time.
Survives the mission: the battery never drops below 140 Wh (lowest 622 Wh).
Longest darkness 11 h: that is the cold soak.
Battery used on this mission: 78 Wh of the 560 Wh it can use above its 140 Wh floor.
Battery model: power = panel power x visible Sun, whatever the Sun's direction (a sun-tracking array), so survival is an upper bound for fixed panels.
why: Marginal touchdown: the top of Earth's disc clears the skyline by under 0.5 deg; Earth is 0.04 deg above the skyline (bearing 153 deg, set by the Moon's own curvature at -0.70 deg), so there is almost no margin for a landing error, a lower antenna or a later hour.
Darkest spell from 2028-10-27T00 UTC (11 h): terrain 4.5 km away blocks it (bearing 218 deg: skyline 1.36 deg, centre of the body at 1.17 deg).
Longest Earth blackout from 2028-11-07T15 UTC (2 h): it is below the Moon's own curvature (bearing 140 deg, horizon -1.72 deg).
